articles.title: do headless setups actually perform better than traditional ones?
articles.excerpt: I'm on the SRE team at a fashion retailer with 4 brands, and we're partway through moving the storefronts off our old monolith onto a Next.js frontend with Scayle as the multi-brand backend (Shopify Plus with Hydrogen was the other option we priced), with the first 2 brands already live… Product and category pages got a lot faster after the move, and when I dug into the traces, most of the gain lines up with those pages now coming straight from the edge cache. That makes it hard to tell our CTO how much of the win comes from headless itself and how much from caching we could have added to the old stack too, which matters because the next 2 brands are budgeted on the speed argument. So for those who measured before and after a headless move, how much of the speedup was left once caching was set up the same way on both?   submitted by   /u/Spiritual-Pen-905 [link]   [comments]
articles.summary: Le passage en headless a accéléré les pages produit/catégorie via le cache edge, mais difficile de distinguer l'impact réel du headless de celui du caching.
